title: Uniform Tor intervals for finite constant p-adic scalar models
statement: Let ell be prime and Lambda a commutative condensed ring isomorphic to Z_ell or O_E, with c=-1, or isomorphic to Q_ell, E, or the finite-subextension-valued algebraic closure, with c=0. Here E ranges over finite subextensions of the fixed p-adic algebraic closure. For every scheme S and every Lambda_S-module N admitting a finite constant local model [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model], the degree-zero complex N[0] has Tor amplitude [c,0] [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude]. No finiteness hypothesis on S is imposed.

proof.text: Use finiteConstantLocalModel_iff_exists_cover to express each given condensed finite constant model as finiteConstantScalarExtension of an internal finitely presented module over the ordinary scalar ring Lambda(*). Evaluation at the singleton identifies the scalar ring with the given PID or field. For the finite-subextension-valued algebraic closure, evaluation is bijective: each individual algebraic element lies in the finite extension generated by that element. Transport these scalar identifications along the supplied monoid isomorphism.

For fields, use the ordinary-module equivalence and a finite basis to identify each scalar model with a finite free module. Scalar realization preserves finite free modules. For PIDs, the kernel of a finite free surjection is a finitely generated free module, by the Mathlib PID free-submodule theorem. This gives a short exact sequence with finite free first and second terms.

Prove exactness of the scalar realization by the constant-to-continuous flatness argument specialized to the original Type-0 coefficient rings and arbitrary site universe. Continuous-function modules are torsion-free over the PID, hence flat. Locally lift each finite relation from the constant sheaf to scalar coefficients, and apply the local equational criterion. Transport internal flatness through the section-module equivalence to obtain left exact extension of scalars. Naturality of the constant-sheaf counit, uniqueness of left adjoints, and the monoidal inverse-image adjunction identify realization with constant sheafification, this exact extension, and exact inverse image. Transport along the supplied coefficient isomorphism.

The mapped short exact sequence is represented by the mapping cone of its first map in degree zero. This cone has support in degrees -1 and 0 and dualizable, hence flat, terms. Apply the generic internal bounded-flat Tor theorem. In the field cases apply its degree-zero flat-object corollary directly. The proof includes rank zero.

For the original cover, exact restriction commutes with derived tensor via leftDerivedUpperStarTensorIso and with homology. Use the coverHomologyZero and transportTensorIso helpers of LocalModelTorBoundDescent to descend the resulting homology vanishing against every test module. The cover need not have finite index set; the zero-detection helper works for any Scheme.Cover, including an empty cover.

lean.statement:
theorem padic_constant_local_model_tor
    (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime]
    (Λ : Sheaf (coherentTopology Profinite.{u}) Ab.{u + 1}) [MonObj Λ] [IsCommMonObj Λ]
    (c : ℤ)
    (hΛ :
      (c = -1 ∧ (Nonempty (Mon.mk Λ ≅ Mon.mk (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj ℤ_[ℓ])) ∨
        ∃ E : PadicAlgCl.FiniteIntermediateField ℓ,
          Nonempty (Mon.mk Λ ≅ Mon.mk (Profinite.padicIntegersRingObj ℓ E)))) ∨
      (c = 0 ∧ (Nonempty (Mon.mk Λ ≅ Mon.mk (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj ℚ_[ℓ])) ∨
        (∃ E : PadicAlgCl.FiniteIntermediateField ℓ,
          Nonempty (Mon.mk Λ ≅ Mon.mk (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj E))) ∨
        Nonempty (Mon.mk Λ ≅ Mon.mk (Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj ℓ)))))
    (S : Scheme.{u})
    (N : Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology S) Ab.{u + 1}) (condensedRingObj Λ S))
    (hN : HasFiniteConstantLocalModel Λ S N) :
    _root_.DerivedCategory.torAmplitudeIn _ c 0
      ((_root_.DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj N)
